title: ArXiv caps submissions at two per month as AI paper flood overwhelms the preprint server
source_used: The Decoder (fulltext fetched by main session)
key_facts: From 1 Oct 2026 arXiv allows only two submissions per person per calendar month; the existing cap of three active submissions at once, in place since 2024, stays.
The limit applies to the person who submits, not co-authors; rejected papers still count, but deleting a paper before publication returns the slot.

Monthly submissions were 9,869 in September 2016, 20,569 in September 2024 and 40,363 in September 2026; the surge generated nearly 9,000 support tickets, and cs.AI submissions grew more than sixfold in two years.

Thomas G. Dietterich, chair of arXiv's Editorial Advisory Council, says a relatively small proportion of authors submit many low-quality papers and use a disproportionate fraction of volunteer moderators' time.
arXiv calls the rule a temporary fix until its moderation tools can scale; Dietterich hopes the cap can be raised or dropped later.
arXiv tightened rules for computer science papers in November 2025 and announced in May 2026 a one-year ban for authors whose papers clearly contain unverified LLM output.
arXiv has been moving to an independent nonprofit since 1 July 2026; in late September three funders pledged a total of $17.2 million over three to five years.
quote_evidence: Starting October 1, 2026, the preprint platform Arxiv will allow only two submissions per person per calendar month.
Arxiv calls the rule a temporary fix until its own moderation tools can scale.
Dietterich says he hopes the cap can be raised or dropped later.
why_it_matters_hint: arXiv's own figures show submissions doubling in two years, partly from AI tools, and the cap is its stopgap.
event_date: 1 Oct 2026 (cap takes effect); The Decoder published on 11 Oct 2026.
